disclaimer: These statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.
_acceptedDisclaimerVariantsComment: Disclaimer variants ACCEPTED IN PLACE OF `disclaimer` wherever a scan must not read required legal text as copy (C6/C17/C18/C19 and the current-listing audit diff). They are NOT accepted as the disclaimer a generated listing must carry: C5 and A1 compare `fdaDisclaimer` and the description against `disclaimer` verbatim, so generated output written with a variant still hard-fails. The previous name (`auditAcceptDisclaimers`) implied audit-only scope it never had.
acceptedDisclaimerVariants: This statement has not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.
_prescriptionDrugNamesComment: Prescription-drug brand/generic names. Claiming a product replaces or acts like a prescription drug is a DRUG CLAIM, so the gate scans these on the same C6/A2 path (same de-obfuscation passes) as the disease nouns.
negationMetaPhrases: not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease
not intended to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease
does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease
not a substitute for medical advice
_benignContextPhrasesComment: Fixed retail phrases in which a disease word is a CALENDAR reference ("cold and flu season") or an ANATOMY reference ("sinus cavity", "oral cavity" — a body SPACE, not tooth decay), not a claim. A disease-term match INSIDE one of these spans is suppressed; a therapeutic-action verb in the same clause in front of the phrase re-arms it ("prevents colds during cold and flu season" still fails). The anatomy spans are what makes the bare dental nouns cavity/cavities safe to ship in the oral subcategory lexicon.

allergenFields._comment: Attribute keys + phrasing the allergen checks (C9/A7) use. PACK DATA — lib/gate holds no attribute-key or allergen-phrase literals.

_noAllergenCanonical_doc: AM-4a — the CANONICAL none-style allergen declaration.
When the label carries NO declarable allergen the declaration attribute must still
say something, and it must say the SAME thing every time: an empty field reads as
'not answered', and free-text variants ('none', 'N/A', 'no allergens') are
unverifiable — one of them is outright banned. C23 requires the declaration
attribute to equal this string EXACTLY whenever no declarable allergen is present.
INDEPENDENT of C9, which bans `noAllergenPhrases` when an allergen IS present:
'No Known Allergens' stays banned by C9 whatever this value says.
noAllergenCanonical: Free from major allergens per label
_substantiationTokensComment: R33/R38 — the SUBSTANTIATION REGISTER vocabulary, ported from the harness kit's C30. Every certification/origin/quality claim in customer copy needs an ARTIFACT behind it, and the original project shipped 'cGMP-certified, third-party-tested' live on three surfaces with no register entry anywhere: every other check asked 'is this phrasing allowed?', none asked 'can we prove it?'. Each row is [regexSource, displayName]. ADVISORY ONLY — it builds audit.substantiationRegister for operator sign-off and can never fail a run, which is why it is not a REQUIRED_PACK_PIECE.
_candidateTermHeuristicsComment: brain/02 — the CANDIDATE-NOUN proposer. ADVISORY: it scans the SOURCE listing for condition-like terms this pack's lexicon does not know and proposes them to whoever owns the lexicon. It exists because a blind spot cannot report itself: the oral/dental nouns were missing for months and no run could say so. `medicalSuffixes` are morphological endings that mark a medical noun; `therapeuticVerbCues` are the verbs whose OBJECT is worth proposing; `stopwords` are words that are never candidates however they are shaped. Never a failure, so never a REQUIRED_PACK_PIECE.
_ingredientSubsetRuleComment: C26 — the ACTIVE-vs-FULL ingredient attribute pair. Every ingredient named in `subsetKey` must appear in `supersetKey`: an active ingredient missing from the full label list is either a copy error or an undeclared ingredient, and Amazon's ingredient-match enforcement reads both from the same panel. Comparison is TOLERANT of formatting (case, punctuation, ordering, amounts and parentheticals are all normalized away) because the two fields are legitimately written in different styles; it fails only when a word of the active ingredient's NAME appears nowhere in the full list. Emptying this disarms C26, so it is a REQUIRED_PACK_PIECE.
_allergenDeclarationSurfacesComment: AM-3 — which SURFACES C9 requires the allergen declaration on. DEFAULT IS THE FULL TRIPLE DECLARATION: attribute AND description AND at least one bullet; that is what ships here and what every existing check enforces. The key exists only so an operator whose category genuinely cannot carry the bullet leg can drop THAT leg for their own pack — the override is DEFAULT OFF (every flag true). `attribute` and `description` may NEVER be switched off: REQUIRED_PACK_PIECES raises a blocking PACK failure if either is false, so this flag can never become a way to disarm C9 wholesale. Separate from, and no weakening of, the POSITION rule (rules.bulletArchitecture.allergenPosition), which says the bullet's declaration must TRAIL rather than lead.

promptRules._comment: Category-specific generation guidance injected into the prompts. PACK DATA — lib/engine/prompts holds no category lexicon.
promptRules._complianceComment: The COMPLIANCE headline rules. These used to be hard-coded English sentences inside lib/engine/prompts/system.ts; they are pack data now so the engine carries no category rule text.
compliance: NEVER claim to diagnose, treat, cure, prevent, or mitigate any disease or symptom.
NEVER claim the product replaces, matches, or acts like a prescription drug.
No price, discount, shipping or availability statement in copy.
promptRules._titleComment: R33/R38 — the header fields (title, title75, itemHighlights) carry no UNEVIDENCED trust claim. The substantiation register reports one that slips through; this is the prevention half.
title: Do NOT put an origin, certification, testing or heritage claim (country of origin, manufacturing standard, third-party testing, dietary certification, years in business, units sold) in the title or Item Highlights unless the CURRENT LISTING above already carries it. Every such claim needs an artifact behind it, the header fields are the ones a moderator reads first, and a claim the source listing never made is one nobody has evidence for.
Keep the header fields to what the product IS: identity, form, count, the primary keyword cluster and audience qualifiers.
system: Do NOT write the disclaimer anywhere — the system inserts the verbatim constant itself. Claim-bearing bullets end with a trailing "*" marker only.
If an allergen is present, declare it exactly as "Contains: [Allergen]" consistently; never write "No Known Allergens" when one is present.
attributes: "active_ingredients" must be a subset of "ingredients" (actives only; full label list in ingredients) — every active is checked against the full list.

NEVER put a strength/potency figure in an attribute whose name is about dose (dosage, strength, potency): structured data states the number AS a dose. Give the maximum dose as a COUNT of the dosage form, and keep the strength figure in copy attached to the blend or formula.
"allergen_information": exact canonical string if an allergen is present, else "Free from major allergens per label" ONLY if the label says so, else omit.
"legal_disclaimer_description": write the literal string "[SYSTEM_DISCLAIMER]" — the system replaces it.
bullets: One bullet must declare the allergen ("Contains: ...") if any allergen is present in the ingredients; if none, one bullet covers quality/testing signals instead.
description: Cover: what it is, who it's for, how to use, quality/safety (including "Contains: [Allergen]" if applicable and a short safety note: pregnancy/nursing/physician consult/keep from children).
qa: Cover: usage, timing, who it's for, dietary/allergen, storage, what makes it different, results expectations (compliant phrasing).
aplus: In the ingredients/feature module, declare "Contains: [Allergen]" if an allergen is applicable.

_actionPairedNounsComment: Terms that are NOT diseases on their own and must only fail when a therapeutic-ACTION verb sits in the same sentence. 'menopause'/'perimenopause' are enumerated NATURAL STATES under 21 CFR 101.93(g), so 'Formulated for women in perimenopause and menopause' is a lawful structure/function claim and blocking it blocked tens of thousands of lawful listings; 'cures menopause' still fails. 'nash' collides with a common surname and place name. Scanned by the same C6/A2 path, gated on the pack's own action-verb class.
_naturalStatesComment: NATURAL STATES ARE NOT DISEASES (21 CFR 101.93(f)/(g) and the FDA Small Entity Compliance Guide for the structure/function rule). Ageing, menopause, the menstrual cycle, adolescence and pregnancy are natural states or processes, not diseases, even though each can be ASSOCIATED with abnormal conditions that are. FDA's line is: NORMAL SYMPTOMOLOGY of a natural state is permissible; an ABNORMAL condition is not. A term listed here is therefore NEVER a violation on its own — 'supports comfort during menopause' and 'formulated for women in perimenopause and menopause' are lawful structure/function copy. It becomes a disease claim only when C22 finds (a) an abnormality marker beside it, or (b) a therapeutic-action verb in the same sentence with no lawful qualifier. Bare 'period' is deliberately NOT listed: as a natural-state token it collides with 'return period', 'trial period' and 'period of time' far more often than it names the menstrual cycle, and 'menstrual period' / 'monthly period' / 'menstruation' / 'menstrual cycle' / 'pms' already carry the doctrine.
_normalSymptomologyNounsComment: NORMAL SYMPTOMOLOGY whose UNQUALIFIED form names a disease. The second half of the same FDA rule: 'helps prevent the mild memory loss associated with aging' is FDA's own worked example of a permissible structure/function claim, while an unqualified promise to prevent memory loss is a claim about dementia. Terms here ride BOTH C22 rules — the abnormality-marker rule AND the therapeutic-action rule — so the mild/occasional/associated-with framing is required before an action verb may touch them. 'memory loss' was moved here out of `diseaseNounsBySubcategory.brain` because holding it as a flat disease noun blocked FDA's own example; the abnormal forms it used to stand in for ('dementia', 'alzheimer's', 'vascular dementia', 'cognitive decline') are all still flat disease nouns, so nothing that was blocked as a DISEASE is now permitted.
_abnormalOnlySymptomNounsComment: NORMAL SYMPTOMOLOGY that a structure/function claim MAY lawfully address. FDA treats the normal symptomology of a natural state as permissible, so 'helps with hot flashes' is not by itself a disease claim — only the ABNORMAL form is. Terms here are therefore scanned by the abnormality-marker rule ONLY ('severe hot flashes', 'chronic sleeplessness', 'clinical mood swings' fail); the therapeutic-action rule deliberately does NOT apply, because acting on a normal symptom is exactly what a lawful structure/function claim does and applying it would block widespread lawful copy for no regulatory gain.
_abnormalityMarkersComment: ABNORMALITY MARKERS — the words that push a natural state or a normal symptom over the line into an abnormal condition, which IS a disease claim. Two C22 rules use them: (1) a marker within `naturalStateProximityWindow` characters of a natural state / normal symptom makes that phrase a disease claim ('severe menopause symptoms', 'clinical memory loss'); (2) two DIFFERENT markers inside the same window name an abnormal condition outright ('diagnosed medical condition', 'chronic mood disorder'). A lawful qualifier NEVER rescues a marker — the precedence is disease noun > abnormality marker > lawful qualifier.
_lawfulQualifiersComment: THE SAFE-HARBOUR SIDE. These are the qualifiers FDA's guidance uses to keep a natural-state claim lawful: the mild/occasional/normal form, the 'already within the normal range' construction, and the 'associated with [natural state]' connector. They do TWO things and nothing more: (a) inside C22 they suppress the therapeutic-action-verb rule when no abnormality marker is present, which is what keeps 'helps prevent mild memory loss associated with aging' lawful while 'cures aging' fails; (b) they are injected into the generation prompt as approved phrasing. They are NOT a licence to name a disease — a listed disease noun is failed by C6 whatever qualifier surrounds it, so 'mild alzheimer's' and 'age-related macular degeneration' still hard-fail. Emptying this list makes the gate STRICTER, not weaker, which is why it is not a required manifest piece.
_naturalStateSafePhrasesComment: FALSE-POSITIVE REDUCER for C22 only. These spans are blanked out (length-preserving) before the natural-state scan runs, exactly as `semanticDrugClaims.safeContextPhrases` are blanked before C21. They cover the two contexts in which an abnormality marker is ordinary retail or safety language rather than a claim: research vocabulary ('clinical study', 'clinically tested') and the standard consult-a-professional warning ('if you have a diagnosed medical condition, consult your physician'). THE QUALIFIER SLOT IS ENUMERATED, NEVER WILDCARDED: a live run on B00IO89MYA wrote the MANDATED safety warning (the `safety_warning` attribute is REQUIRED by the attribute template) as 'If you are pregnant, nursing, have a known medical condition, or take medication' and C22 R1 failed it, because 'have a diagnosed medical condition' and 'have a medical condition' were both listed while 'have a KNOWN medical condition' was not — the same required warning, one adjective different, and no repair could clear it without deleting text the template requires. The ordinary qualifiers a safety warning puts in that slot are listed beside them. Blanking stays span-local: it never rescues a marketing claim written outside one of these phrases, so 'for diagnosed medical conditions' and 'for known medical conditions' both still fail. Emptying it makes the gate stricter.
naturalStateSafePhrases: if you have a diagnosed medical condition
if you have a known medical condition
_advisoryComment: FALSE-POSITIVE REDUCER for C22 R3 only (never a manifest piece — emptying these makes the gate STRICTER, not weaker). A sentence that pairs one of `advisoryCueVerbs` with one of `advisoryProfessionalNouns` (cue first, professional within the adjacency gap) is an ADVISORY — the mandated consult-a-professional safety warning — not a product claim, so R3's therapeutic-action rule does not fire on a natural state inside it ("Women who are pregnant or nursing … should talk with a physician"). Scope, stated exactly: the escape covers R3 alone; abnormality markers (R1/R2), the C6 disease-noun scan and the C6 action-paired tier are untouched, and the escape is DENIED when a therapeutic-action verb shares the state's own comma-bounded clause segment — "reverses aging, talk to your doctor" still fails because "reverses" sits in the same segment as "aging".
_approvedClaimTemplatesComment: THE PREVENTION HALF. Lawful structure/function claim SHAPES from the FDA guidance — a statement about the role of a nutrient or ingredient in affecting normal structure or function, or the mechanism by which it maintains that structure or function. Rendered into the system prompt by `buildSystemPrompt` so the generator writes compliant copy by construction rather than being repaired into it. Bracketed slots are placeholders the model fills from the product's own facts.
approvedClaimTemplates: helps maintain [parameter] already within the normal range
helps support [structure] as part of a balanced diet
helps prevent mild [symptom] associated with [natural state]
_allergenCompoundExclusionsComment: Compounds whose NAME contains an allergen source word but which are not that allergen. Blanked out of the label text BEFORE the allergen-source scan, so 'Milk Thistle Extract' no longer produces a demand to write 'Contains: Milk' on the label and 'Gluten Free Oat Fibre' no longer produces 'Contains: Wheat'. Pack data — the gate holds no ingredient literals.
_ingredientAttributeKeysComment: Attribute keys that carry the per-ingredient breakdown. C12 accepts a potency figure that is ATTRIBUTED to a named ingredient only when the same number+unit appears in one of these attributes; an attributed figure that appears nowhere in them is still measured against facts.potency. PACK DATA — the gate names no attribute key.

semanticDrugClaims._comment: SEMANTIC DRUG-CLAIM heuristics (gate C21). A drug claim does not need a disease noun or a banned verb: 'shrinks the lump in your breast', 'ends the need for dialysis' and 'so you can throw away your inhaler' contain none of either. Three PROXIMITY rules are compiled from these lists at load time (pathological verb near an anatomical target; a replacement cue near a therapy/device noun; a restoration verb near a lost-function noun), plus the literal `patterns` below. Everything here is PACK DATA — lib/gate compiles it and holds no term of its own. The scan runs over the SAME additive de-obfuscation variant set the prohibited-content scans use (homoglyph/small-caps fold, leetspeak, doubled letters, separator collapse and the separator-stripped variant), so `shr1nks the lump` and `sh rinks the lump` fail too. `safeContextPhrases` are blanked out first so genuine SAFETY copy ('do not stop taking your medication', 'not a substitute for prescription medication') is never reported. CONTEXT-QUALIFIED TARGETS: a target entry may be an object with `requiresContext` (the term counts only when one of those words is within the proximity window) or `benignContext` (the term is cleared when one of those words is). That is how 'plaque' distinguishes 'clears the plaque out of your arteries' (a drug claim) from 'removes the plaque from your teeth' (lawful oral care), and how 'the growth' distinguishes a tumour from 'restores the growth of your hair'. Plain strings stay unconditional targets.
patterns: claim that a physician will withdraw or reduce a prescribed therapy
claim that the buyer can stop taking a prescribed therapy
ICD diagnosis code (a diagnosis reference is a disease claim)
